approved: Family Assistance Legislation Amendment (Child Care Measures) Bill (No. 2) 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would freeze the income thresholds for the Child Care Benefit at their 30 June 2014 levels for three years from 1 July 2014.
It amends the A New Tax System (Family Assistance) Act 1999 to stop indexation of those thresholds until 1 July 2017.
The standard hourly rate, minimum hourly amount and multiple child loadings for the Child Care Benefit would still be indexed each year by the Consumer Price Index.
Freezes Child Care Benefit income thresholds at 30 June 2014 amounts for three income years starting 1 July 2014.
Defers the first indexation of these thresholds to 1 July 2017.
Maintains annual CPI indexation of the Child Care Benefit standard hourly rate, minimum hourly amount and multiple child loadings.
Families receiving the Child Care Benefit.

Introduced a bill maintaining Child Care Benefit income thresholds for three years to save an estimated $230 million, and cited a NATSEM report finding childcare fees rose 53 per cent under the previous Labor government, with out-of-pocket costs up by as much as 40 per cent in its last four years.
